analysis: The PR adds a `purpose` (provider | desktop_account) to the console device-code approval flow. `link/page.tsx` line 8 reads it from the `?purpose=` query string. `DeviceLinkForm.tsx` line 45 sends it in the POST body to `/api/device/approve`. The route handler is unchanged and passes the body through, per docs/architecture/components/console-ui.md. Authorization of the purpose, the 30-day scope and its revocation are enforced only in the coordinator, which is outside this repo and unverified here. The UI check at line 62 runs after approval, which is the main concern (A-008, TB-002). Concerns for the next pass: the coordinator must reject a purpose mismatch and a missing purpose before it approves; confirm the desktop token cannot be used where provider tokens are accepted (TB-002 provider registration); and check that A-008 and the doc cover the new token type. The change touches no cache, attestation or encryption paths (T-041 unaffected). `console-ui.md` is documentation only. The Privy Bearer forwarding is unchanged.

findings.detail: `handleSubmit` posts `purpose` to `/api/device/approve` and checks `data.purpose` only after the coordinator has returned success (line 62). The server-side approval has already happened by then. If the coordinator build is older or lacks strict purpose enforcement, it ignores the field. A victim opening `/link?purpose=desktop_account` with an attacker-supplied provider-flow code would then link the attacker's provider to the victim's account. The UI shows 'did not confirm read-only desktop access, try again after it is updated', which wrongly implies nothing was granted. This matters for A-008 and TB-002 because a hostile provider could receive the account's earnings assignment. Fix: gate rollout on coordinator enforcement, and tell the user the approval may have taken effect and must be revoked. The coordinator should reject mismatched purposes before approving, and it must treat a missing `purpose` as provider-only.
findings.title: Desktop-scope check runs only after approval, so a coordinator that ignores `purpose` still links the device

findings.detail: The UI now tells users that `desktop_account` approval grants 30-day access to view Macs and earnings and cannot start providers, manage API keys or withdraw funds (line 217). The purpose is also taken from a URL query parameter (`page.tsx` line 8), so a crafted link can change the page's wording and the purpose sent. The enforcement lives in the coordinator, which is outside this repo. A-008 covers only provider tokens. The new token type, its lifetime, scope enforcement, revocation, and the phishing path through `?purpose=` have no asset, threat or mitigation entry. Add these to the threat model, and verify that the server enforces the purpose binding and the scope limits the UI promises.
findings.title: New 30-day read-only desktop credential and its scope claims are not covered by the threat model
